title: Time-lapse Fluorescence Imaging of Arabidopsis Root Growth with Rapid Manipulation of The Root Environment Using The RootChip
protocol: Fill a 10 cm Petri dish with growth medium containing 1% agar to a thickness of 5 mm.
Use a multi-channel pipette to fill 10 μl pipette tips with 5 μl of medium from the Petri dish while the medium is still liquid.
Store the filled tips in the pipette tip box until the medium solidifies, then cut them into 4 mm long plastic cones.
Place the plastic cones upright into a Petri dish containing solid growth medium.
Surface sterilize seeds in 5% NaOCl for 5 min.
Wash the seeds three times with sterile water.
Place a single seed on top of each of the medium-filled cones.
Seal the dish with Micropore tape and store at 4 °C to synchronize germination.
Transfer the plates to a growth cabinet after three days.
Maintain the conditions at 23 °C with a 16h high light/8h dark cycle (light intensity: 100 μE m-2 s-1).
Check seedling health, root length, and expression of any fluorescent marker under a dissecting microscope between 5 and 7 days after germination.
Mark individual seedlings for transfer onto the chip.
Select ten or so seedlings to account for potential damage during transfer.
Sterilize the RootChip for long-term experiments using tissue paper and autoclaving.
Cover the cooled RootChip with liquid growth medium, ensuring it is completely immersed but not more than 3 mm above the surface.
Pull medium through the root inlet and chamber outlet using a 20 μl pipette to fill the observation chamber.
Plug plastic cones into the RootChip inlets, fitting them snugly without applying too much pressure.
Incubate the RootChip overnight in liquid medium with two glass slides placed on it to prevent floating.
Add a magnetic stir bar and close the Petri dish.
Transfer the assembly to a magnetic stirrer and gently agitate the medium.
Tilt the assembly slightly by placing a glass slide under the Petri dish on the side opposite of the outlets.
Maintain light/dark cycle by illuminating seedlings with a ring lamp set at 100 μE m-2 s-1 connected to a timer.
Fill a sealable, pressurizable vial with liquid growth medium.
Invert the chip carrier and place it on a stable surface.
Remove the RootChip from the liquid medium and insert it PDMS side down into the bottom aperture of the chip carrier.
Orient the RootChip so that the side containing the control layer inlets faces the side of the pressure line tubing connectors in the carrier wall.
Dry the cover glass on the bottom of the chip by gently blotting with tissue paper.
Secure the RootChip to the carrier with tape and right the whole assembly.
Cut flexible plastic microbore tubing into 5 cm long pieces.
Connect the tubing pieces to stainless steel microbore tubes.
Fill the tubing connectors with water using a syringe.
Plug each tubing connector into the corresponding control layer inlet on the chip.
Plug the opposite ends of the lines into the media/solution vial(s).
Apply pressure to the solution vial with a syringe of air.
Place the carrier onto the microscope stage.
Fit the carrier exactly into the notches of the stage insert.
Close both pressure regulators before connecting the chip.
Add a few ml of water to the reservoirs of the carrier.
Repeat adding water to the reservoirs over the course of longer experiments.
Keep the volume low in the reservoirs to minimize liquid spillage onto the microscope.
Connect the chip outlets to the reservoirs with microbore tubing for long-term experiments if necessary.
Collect outflow that accumulates on the chip surface by pipetting when needed.
Prepare squared sheets of transparent plastic from sheet protectors.
Fix the transparent plastic to the carrier by double-sided tape.
Position the ring light over the chip.
Maintain the light/dark cycle.
Switch off the ring light prior to experiments using fluorescent markers.
Download the RootChip controller interface for LabView software from the website.
Close the valves on the chip by applying pressure through the control layer.
Activate all three solution-inlet valves in the controller interface.
Open the pressure regulators.
Open the pressure regulator for the control layer and set to 15 psi.
Open the pressure regulator for the flow layer and set to 5 psi.
Open the inlet valve for the growth medium to flush the chambers with medium.
Check flow paths under the microscope to remove air from the channels.
Flush each of the eight chambers several times at 5 psi until all air is forced out.
Flush the RootChip chambers with dark food coloring diluted 1:4 in hydroponic medium.
Measure fluid exchange within the chambers under recommended pressure of 5 psi.
Observe root growth in seedlings supplied with 10 mM Glucose as an external energy source.
Monitor intracellular glucose and galactose levels in roots expressing genetically encoded nanosensors using Förster Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET).
Perfuse roots in the chip with square pulses of glucose or galactose solution.
Measure intracellular sugar levels by monitoring intensity ratios between acceptor fluorophore Citrine and donor ECFP.
